clue.text: Continued with the ironing?

parts.note: to keep going is to persevere; with an iron, cloth that has been flattened by pressure has had the iron put on it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the household chores carried on, the iron still in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means kept going, and read literally describes clothes that have had the iron pushed down onto them.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for persevering or carrying on regardless, literally describing flattened laundry.

clue.text: Policeman held up in a state of terror

indicators.note: the policeman has held the other letters within him

parts.note: PC is police constable

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word in is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: An officer is caught in a frightening situation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses 'in'; 'held' says the policeman's letters hold it and 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming fear or alarm is a synonym.

clue.text: Propagates fresh greens — about to finish

indicators.note: the rearranged vegetables go about the other word
a fresh version of the word greens is a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: to end is to finish

explanation.surface: Vegetables that grow anew are about to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges greens to ENGERS, and 'about' wraps that round the word for finish; the dash is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about or produce is to beget, a synonym.

clue.text: Community payment

definitions.meaning: a village or colony of people living together
a sum paid to clear a debt or claim

explanation.definitionFit: A colony or newly founded village, and an agreed sum paid in a legal case.

clue.text: It's no way to address a lady!

definitions.text: It's no way to address a lady!

parts.words: It's no way to address a lady!
parts.note: the standard opening for a letter to a man, wrong for a woman

explanation.surface: An exclamation at rudeness towards a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' suggests speech or manners, but it is the salutation that starts a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal salutation opening a letter to a man, quite unsuitable for writing to Madam.

clue.text: 9 to 5, he goes round the old city

parts.note: the number nine written out
V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: the word he is turned round, written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone working nine to five tours an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: '9 to 5' reads as office hours; it gives NINE then V.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of ancient Assyria, on the Tigris, is a ruined city of antiquity.

clue.text: He took the hat round for not much money

indicators.note: the hat goes round the other word, enclosing it like a container

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A busker or collector passed the hat round and raised very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took the hat round' suggests a collection, but 'round' is the container signal, with 'took' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying something at low cost is buying it on the cheap; the adverbial sense matches the phrase.

clue.text: Not a fair copy

parts.note: a fair copy is a neat final draft, but here fair means honest: a pupil's illicit copied work

explanation.walkthrough: 'fair copy' is a neat final version; read it as an honest copy, and a cheat's copy is not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Copied work used dishonestly, as in an exam, is plagiarism, not honest.

clue.text: Priest and Old Testament poet

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A clergyman and the Bible's first part, together with a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot wrote The Waste Land; George Eliot too, though a novelist.

clue.text: Put off, but not deterred

parts.note: put off can mean discouraged, but here it is delay to a later date, which does not cancel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' looks like discouraged; the clue says it is delayed instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Delayed to a later date or rescheduled, rather than abandoned.

clue.text: Near to the start of darkness

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word, to, is used

explanation.surface: Something is approaching the onset of dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the start of darkness' looks like D, but 'the start of' governs 'to'; darkness is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between dusk and dawn are the night, a direct synonym.

clue.text: May they keep aunties in change?

definitions.text: May they keep aunties in change?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed around into a new order

parts.note: the fodder taken as written
the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether pensions will keep elderly relatives in pocket money.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: regular payments that keep aunties supplied with cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearly fixed payments, often bought for retirement, provide pocket money for older relatives.

clue.text: Convincing vice-consul is difficult

indicators.note: a difficult person is awkward, so the letters are put into an awkward new order

explanation.surface: A deputy diplomat being awkward is a persuasive one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' is the anagram signal; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof that settles a matter beyond doubt is decisive, so it convinces.

clue.text: Finish roadwork

parts.note: the road part gives ST, short for street
the work part gives OP, short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A short instruction to wrap up the road repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roadwork' looks like one word, but splits into road and work, each abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: To end or cease an activity is a direct synonym of finish.

clue.text: Proverbially, it leads to madness!

parts.note: the saying runs that what is unseen is followed by being 'out of mind', taken jokingly as insanity

explanation.walkthrough: In the proverb this phrase is followed by 'out of mind', which means forgotten; read as 'mad' it becomes the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden from view; the proverb says being unseen leads to being forgotten, or 'out of mind'.

clue.text: The craft of the cook?

parts.note: craft here means a boat, not a skill; a kitchen pan for cooking over vapour shares its name with a steam-driven ship

explanation.surface: Asking about the art or skill of cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' reads as skill but means a vessel; the boat is the cook's utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam-powered ship is a vessel, and a pan for cooking vegetables over boiling water.

clue.text: Puts an end to current measures in beer

indicators.note: the electrical units go in the beer word

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
amps measure electric current

explanation.surface: Electrical units in a pint end something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is electric current, so its units are amps.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush or extinguish, like a fire under foot, is to bring something to an end.

clue.text: Sweetheart lost by doctor and poet

indicators.note: the letter is dropped from the doctor's title, lost from it

parts.note: a houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain
the heart, or middle letter, of sweet is E

explanation.surface: A medic loses his love, along with a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: A houseman is a British junior hospital doctor. A. E. Housman wrote A Shropshire Lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Housman was an English writer of verse, author of A Shropshire Lad.

clue.text: Employ recruit

definitions.meaning: to enlist someone for a purpose

explanation.definitionFit: To put to use, and to enlist someone to help, both mean using a resource.

clue.text: Agrees when ordered to go aboard a ship

indicators.note: the word put aboard the vessel goes inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
someone ordered to go has been sent

explanation.surface: Someone consents when told to board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; the word for ordered to go sits between the ship's two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent or concur is a synonym, as in he assents to the plan.

clue.text: Takes Mickey to prison?

parts.note: taking the mickey is British slang for mocking; in the US, jailing someone is also this phrase

explanation.walkthrough: 'take the mickey' is British slang for mock; 'Mickey' looks like a person, and the American phrase for jailing someone is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocks or parodies someone, and in American usage puts them in jail.

clue.text: Warped, like the criminal mind

definitions.meaning: bent or twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A twisted mind, like a criminal's.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent out of shape, and dishonest in the manner of a crook or villain.

clue.text: Is inclined to enter the church, subject to purification

indicators.note: the leaning word goes to enter the church letters, inside them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans means is inclined

explanation.surface: Someone tends to go into church for spiritual purification.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To purify or wash thoroughly, a verb sense matching the phrase.

clue.text: Settled one into residence

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the dwelling word

parts.note: a pad is informal for a home or flat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone settled into their new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' reads as moved in, but it means a bill was cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that has been settled has been paid off in full.

clue.text: Deduce there's no getting away from Hades

indicators.note: the word no is getting away from the underworld word, removed from it

parts.note: an inferno is hell, the underworld

explanation.surface: Concluding that nobody can escape the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no getting away' reads as inescapable, but 'no' is the letters dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude from evidence or reasoning is a synonym.

clue.text: Reserve player

parts.note: a substitute in the theatre who learns a role in case the lead actor cannot go on

explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests sport, but it is an actor kept in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre substitute who learns a lead part in case the actor is unable to perform.

clue.text: An off-peak call?

parts.note: off-peak suggests a cheap phone call, but here it is a cry sent out from a mountain peak

explanation.walkthrough: 'off-peak call' reads as a cheap telephone call; it is an Alpine singer's cry off a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The warbling Alpine cry of Swiss or Tyrolean singers, heard across mountains.

clue.text: Operators of locks and harbours, say

indicators.note: say signals the harbour word is spoken, matching another word's sound

parts.note: quays are harbour wharves

explanation.surface: People who run canal locks and harbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests canals, beside harbours, but they are door locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices turned in locks to open them, so they operate the mechanism.

clue.text: Switch positions round the oceans, when business is slack

indicators.note: the two switch settings are placed round the waters, one on each side

parts.note: a switch is either off
or a switch is on
the seas are the oceans

explanation.surface: Someone changes jobs on a cruise ship when trade is quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch positions' looks like a verb phrase, but names the two settings a switch can have, placed either side of the oceans.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet part of the year for resorts and tourist trade, when few visitors come.

clue.text: Consented to give up a vice

indicators.note: the word consented is made to give up the letter, dropping it

parts.note: agreed means consented

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to abandon a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is one of the seven deadly sins, so a vice.

clue.text: They go round on wheels

parts.note: rubber casings fitted round the rims of wheels, which also turn

explanation.surface: Something that travels round on wheels, like a merry-go-round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' suggests travelling, but they are literally fitted round wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber casings fitted around car or bike rims, encircling them.

clue.text: More than enough to fill up ten skips

indicators.note: skips means jumps about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Rubbish to load ten skips is abundant; a skip is a British builder's waste container.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is a large open bin for rubbish in Britain; here 'skips' is the anagram signal, with 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant or ample supply means there is a surplus beyond what is needed.
